title: Thrift routing: tenant spend ceilings with GPU-class affinity and spot hedging
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Design and implement a per-tenant "thrift" routing layer that enforces spend ceilings while maximizing SLO adherence. The feature combines: (1) tenant spend ceilings (soft and hard), (2) GPU-class affinity to prefer cheaper/more efficient accelerators for eligible requests, (3) predictive spot-eviction hedging and bidirectional fallback to on-demand, and (4) graceful model-variant degradation (quantized/compact variants) as a last-resort when budget constraints or capacity pressure prevents preferred placement. Goal: give tenant admins a predictable spend floor/ceiling and SREs deterministic behavior under spot preemption without causing sudden P99 latency spikes or silent quality regressions.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Aisha Khatri created initial PRD and sketched control flow for thrift routing. Proposed soft vs hard spend ceilings and per-tenant tokens.

2026-03-02 - Architecture review with runtime team. Decided to implement spend enforcement in the routing service (not the allocator) to reduce cross-service churn. Runtime will expose GPU-class capability vectors via /capabilities API.
2026-03-05 - Prototype evaluated on staging: per-tenant soft cap throttles requests by 30% under synthetic peak; no noticeable P99 regressions when combined with compact-model fallback.
2026-03-10 - Security and billing teams requested audit hooks for cap hits and explicit log events for customer-facing billing ties. Added instrumentation plan.
2026-03-13 - Implementing tenant quota cache and offline simulation harness. Marcus Nguyen picked up PR for allocator integration.
Next steps - finish allocator integration tests, add rollback canary, and run a 72-hour soak on dedicated customers with nonzero spend ceilings.
acceptance_criteria: Admin UI / API allows setting per-tenant soft_cap and hard_cap (USD/hour) and priority for GPU-class affinity.
Routing service enforces soft_cap with probabilistic throttling policy documented and tunable; hard_cap rejects or routes to fallback depending on policy.
When preferred GPU-class is unavailable or spot eviction probability exceeds threshold, router hedges to on-demand or compact model variants based on configured policy.
No customer sees >10% increase in tail latency compared to baseline when routed to compact variant; quality regression monitored via prompt set and must be within defined thresholds.
Audit events emitted for each cap transition (approaching, soft-enforced, hard-enforced) and surfaced in Console cost dashboards.
Automated integration tests and a 72-hour soak run in staging validating behavior under synthetic spot-evictions and regional capacity skews.
implementation_notes: Routing decision flow: tenant_quota_check -> gpu_class_filter -> spot_risk_score -> fallback_plan -> emit_audit_event -> route_request.
Spot risk score: combine market-derived eviction rate, local recent evictions, and tenant-configured risk_tolerance. Use EWMA over 1, 5, 15 minute windows.

Throttling algorithm: soft_cap uses proportional probabilistic sampler with restart window to avoid synchronized bursts. Soft hits return 429 with 'x-redwood-thrift' header when configured; can be replaced with queueing later.
GPU-class affinity: define capability vector (fp16/ampere/rtx-like) and a cost multiplier; policy engine matches requests to cheapest class within latency SLO.
Fallback model variants: prioritized list per-model (full_fp16 -> q4_0 -> q4_1_compact -> distilled). All variants must register quality deltas in model-metadata service for runtime decisions.
Billing linkage: cap enforcement writes a billing_event record to billing stream for reconciliation; soft-enforced throttles flagged for customer notifications.
Operational metrics: cap_level{tenant}, cap_hits_total, cap_rejections_total, fallback_invocations_total, avg_spot_risk_score, p99_latency_by_route, quality_regression_alerts_by_tenant.
Graceful degradation: when hard_cap reached and 'deny' policy is false, route to the cheapest compatible model variant; if none, reject with clear error code and guidance.
Data retention & privacy: keep cap-related audit logs for 90 days by default; provide opt-in extended retention for enterprise customers.
followups: PM: add tenant-facing UX for cap alerts and override controls (follow-up ticket PM-4982).
SRE: bake into runbook for spot-eviction incidents; add automated mitigation that flips on hedging for top 10% tenants by traffic.
DX: include migration guide for customers who previously relied on global spend guards.
Post-launch: collect 30-day telemetry and run a quality regression sweep tied to Redwood Optimize suggestions.
